name: George F. L. Charles Airport
before:
Saint Lucia's second airport, and the one that matters if a client is staying around Castries. It is 2 km north of the capital, against the much longer drive from Hewanorra in the south east.

The trade off is what flies there. This is a turboprop airport, mostly ATR 72s and Dash 8s, with no scheduled jet service at all. Every jet flight into Saint Lucia, transatlantic services included, uses Hewanorra. So a UK client will land at Hewanorra and may use this airport only for onward island hopping.

It handles around 32,000 flights and 394,000 passengers a year, which is a lot of small aircraft.

The setting is part of the appeal. The runway runs parallel to Vigie Beach, which is a destination in its own right. The airport was called Vigie Field until August 1997, when it was renamed after the Saint Lucia politician Sir George Frederick Lawrence Charles, and most people still say Vigie.
after:
Saint Lucia's second airport, and the one that matters if a client is staying around Castries. It is about 3 km north of the centre of the capital, against the much longer drive from Hewanorra in the south east.

The trade off is what flies there. Regional flights use it: interCaribbean lists non-stop flights to Barbados and Dominica. Flights from the UK land at Hewanorra, so a UK client may use this airport only for onward island hopping.

It is named after George Frederick Lawrence Charles, but most people still call it Vigie.

claims.note: OurAirports has exactly two rows for Saint Lucia, both with scheduled service: this one (a medium airport) and Hewanorra (a large one).

claims.inAfter: interCaribbean lists non-stop flights to Barbados and Dominica

claims.claim: flights from the UK land at Hewanorra
claims.inAfter: Flights from the UK land at Hewanorra
claims.note: Was 'Every jet flight into Saint Lucia, transatlantic services included, uses Hewanorra. So a UK client will land at Hewanorra'. The UK CAA's 2025 route table lists St Lucia traffic only at Hewanorra (Gatwick 131,243 and Heathrow 12,839 passengers in 2025), and no row for this airport. The claim about every jet flight rests on Wikipedia alone (cut below).

sources.quote: All jet services into St. Lucia, including transatlantic flights, operate at the present time via Hewanorra International Airport

claims.claim: named after George Frederick Lawrence Charles
claims.inAfter: It is named after George Frederick Lawrence Charles
claims.note: Was 'renamed after the Saint Lucia politician Sir George Frederick Lawrence Charles' in August 1997. The airline and OurAirports use the name George F. L. Charles Airport; the date, the former name Vigie Field, 'politician' and 'Sir' rest on Wikipedia alone (cut below). As at St Kitts and Nevis, no second source says in words that the airport is named after him; the name itself and Wikipedia's statement carry it.

sources.quote: The airport was renamed on 4 August 1997 in honour of Saint Lucia politician Sir George Frederick Lawrence Charles (1916–2004).

claims.claim: turboprop airport, mostly ATR 72s and Dash 8s, no scheduled jet service
claims.wasBefore: This is a turboprop airport, mostly ATR 72s and Dash 8s, with no scheduled jet service at all.
claims.why: An undated Wikipedia paragraph with no current second source for the aircraft mix or the absence of jets: the operator's (SLASPA's) site serves only a web server's default page and its old airport page is a 404, and interCaribbean, whose December 2025 release lists Embraer ERJ145 and Bombardier CRJ900 jets in its fleet as well as turboprops, does not say which aircraft it uses here. Replaced by what two sources support: regional flights use it.

claims.wasBefore: Every jet flight into Saint Lucia, transatlantic services included, uses Hewanorra.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for all jets. The Saint Lucia Tourism Authority's page names the North American airlines but not the airport they use. Softened to the UK flights, which the CAA's table places at Hewanorra.

The naming and the everyday name Vigie are kept (see above).
